sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Objective type questions: two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Traditional media is very useful to deal with sensitive issues of health. (ii) A market, festival, ritual or village fair are situations where traditional communication takes place.
Fill in the blanks: Various governmental bodies like ______ and ______ division use traditional media for creating awareness.
questions.answer: Sangeet Natak Akademi (Song and Drama); Song and Drama.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: There is always a risk of ______ the forms of traditional media while using them for conveying messages on ______ issues.
Fill in the blanks: A ballad is a ______ usually set to music and is often told in the form of a ______.
Fill in the blanks: Ram Lila, the story of ______, is celebrated and performed all over ______ India.
State true or false: Folk theatre is an example of traditional media; traditional media needs advanced technology.
Name any two government bodies promoting traditional media.
questions.answer: Song and Drama Division and Sangeet Natak Akademi (also Lalit Kala Academy).

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain street theatre and its application.
questions.answer: Street theatre combines traditional theatre forms and can be staged anywhere; it uses songs, drama and music to spread messages on child labour, environment, health and women.

questions.q: Write a short note on any one: (i) Demonstrations (ii) Puppetry.
questions.answer: Demonstrations help transfer knowledge and encourage farmers to try new ideas, with story telling and plays at weekly markets. Puppetry combines entertainment with education and treats sensitive topics such as HIV/AIDS.

questions.q: List the situations where traditional communication takes place.
questions.answer: Markets, festivals, rituals, village fairs, social gatherings and celebrations.

questions.q: Why is traditional media useful to deal with sensitive health issues?
questions.answer: Face-to-face communication is not suitable, but a puppet show or play can explain the issue conveniently and effectively.

questions.q: What is a ballad?
questions.answer: A poem usually set to music, often a story told as a song; used for messages on environment or dowry.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Why do we consider traditional media as the most effective tool for cross-cultural communication? Give example.
questions.answer: Performances and fine arts need no language, so they communicate solidarity and friendship through non-verbal communication; e.g. folk dance or a puppet show understood across regions.

questions.q: Explain the role of traditional media in development communication.
questions.answer: They carry messages on health, polio, family planning, education and environment in the people's own forms such as street theatre, ballads and puppetry, face to face and without language barriers, using government bodies like the Song and Drama Division.

questions.q: Discuss the problems faced by traditional media for their survival and how they can be preserved.
questions.answer: Performers leave due to television and lack of financial support, forms are not taught and have no written documentation; support through viewing, learning, and government bodies like Sangeet Natak Akademi and Song and Drama Division can preserve them.
